phases.name: 1. Create, follow, and moderate
phases.description: Define the author write path, social graph, multi-format media, and publish gate.

phases.name: 2. Fan out without a celebrity storm
phases.description: Publish committed events and precompute ordinary-user feed candidates while pulling celebrity posts later.

phases.name: 3. Assemble a personalized read
phases.description: Merge feed candidates, enforce visibility, rank within the latency budget, and handle engagement.

phases.name: 4. Live updates, trends, and operations
phases.description: Deliver new-post hints, aggregate trending signals, and observe scale/failure behavior.

phases.name: 5. Serve trends and review
phases.description: Expose the asynchronously built trend view through the feed read path with moderation and privacy checks.

steps.title: Turn the brief into separate write and read paths
steps.content: The saved exercise asks for text/image/video posts, follows, likes/comments/shares, personalized feeds, real-time updates, trends, moderation, 1B DAU, celebrity accounts, and feeds under 200ms. We will treat <200ms as a regional p95 read target and assume the 1B DAU is a capacity target, not a measured current load. Reads must not synchronously fan out every followed author's latest post; writes must not synchronously copy a celebrity post to millions of followers.

steps.title: Add author clients
steps.content: Web/mobile authors create posts and follow accounts. Readers may be the same people, but the separate reader node later makes the asynchronous feed path visible.

component.label: Author Web & Mobile
component.description: Posts, follows, likes, comments, and shares

properties.purpose: Submit authenticated social commands and upload media using scoped URLs. Design decisions: platforms = web,mobile.

component.highlightReason: Post/follow commands have different consistency and latency needs from feed reads.

steps.title: Add the social API gateway
steps.content: Authenticate writes, apply quotas, and route feed reads to their own service. For abuse and availability, celebrity accounts may have different rate limits but never bypass authorization.

component.label: Social API Gateway
component.description: Authentication, rate limits, and read/write routing

properties.purpose: Authenticate social commands, rate-limit abusive traffic, and route feed requests. Design decisions: rate limits = per-user-and-endpoint.

component.highlightReason: The gateway protects post writes and low-latency reads without storing feed state.

steps.title: Connect author to gateway
steps.content: Authors use HTTPS for post/follow/engagement commands; media bytes later upload directly to object storage through scoped URLs.

connection.label: Authenticated social API
connection.description: Submit posts, follows, likes, comments, and shares over HTTPS.

steps.title: Add the social write service
steps.content: The write service owns post creation, follow/unfollow, and likes/comments/shares. It uses idempotency keys for client retries, authorizes each mutation, and emits committed events. It stores metadata and content references, not large video bytes.

component.label: Social Write Service
component.description: Posts, follows, engagement, and committed events

properties.purpose: Validate and durably apply post, follow, like, comment, and share commands. Design decisions: idempotency key = user_id,client_operation_id; write models = post,follow,like,comment,share.

component.highlightReason: Explicit social writes support every functional interaction in the brief.

steps.title: Route social mutations
steps.content: The gateway passes authenticated commands to the write service; a separate service handles feed reads later.

connection.label: Post / follow / engage
connection.description: Validate social commands with user identity and idempotency ID.

steps.title: Add the canonical post store
steps.content: Store text, author, visibility, media references, moderation state, and engagement records by post ID and author/time access patterns. A new post starts pending; only approved posts are exposed to fanout and reads. Tombstones/visibility changes must invalidate downstream projections.

component.label: Canonical Post Store
component.description: Posts, visibility, moderation state, and engagement records

properties.purpose: Durable post metadata/text and interaction records with moderation and visibility state. Design decisions: partitioning = post_id-and-author-time-index; transactional outbox = true; state = pending,approved,removed.

component.highlightReason: The feed cache is rebuildable; canonical post state is not.

steps.title: Persist a pending post
steps.content: The write service commits the pending post and an idempotency record before replying to the author. Feed distribution waits for approval.

connection.label: Pending post commit
connection.description: Persist post content/metadata and moderation state; do not fan out pending content.

steps.title: Add the follower graph
steps.content: Store follow/unfollow edges and visibility relationships in a partitioned graph projection. Fanout reads follower batches; feed reads use it for celebrity follows and access checks. A follow change must not require rebuilding every historical feed immediately.

component.label: Follower Graph Store
component.description: Follow edges, privacy relationships, and follower batches

properties.purpose: Answer who-follows-whom and visibility checks for fanout and feed reads. Design decisions: partition key = user_id; celebrity follower pagination = true; follow version = true.

component.highlightReason: Follow relationships are a first-class requirement and drive hybrid fanout.

steps.title: Persist follow and unfollow changes
steps.content: The social write service updates graph edges idempotently and emits a change event so cached views can be refreshed.

connection.label: Follow graph mutation
connection.description: Apply authenticated follow/unfollow edges and visibility version changes.

steps.title: Add media object storage
steps.content: Text stays with post metadata; images and videos use scoped uploads to object storage. Keep immutable originals and derived variants. Metadata points to approved objects so a failed upload never creates a broken visible post.

component.label: Media Object Store
component.description: Images, videos, thumbnails, and encoded variants

properties.purpose: Store original and processed image/video objects; publish only verified references. Design decisions: upload = scoped-signed-url; variants = thumbnail,adaptive-video; checksums = true.

component.highlightReason: Media bytes must not overload the post database or feed response path.

steps.title: Issue direct media uploads
steps.content: The write service authorizes a scoped media upload and records its object reference; clients send bytes directly to storage. This arrow is the control-plane capability, not a proxy for video traffic.

connection.label: Signed media upload
connection.description: Authorize bounded image/video upload and retain its checksum/object key.

steps.title: Add moderation and media processing
steps.content: Scan text and uploaded media for policy violations before public distribution. Background workers also create thumbnails and playable video variants; slow video processing leaves the post pending rather than sending an incomplete item to millions of feeds.

component.label: Moderation & Media Workers
component.description: Policy decisions, thumbnails, and video renditions

properties.purpose: Approve/reject content and produce validated media variants before public feed publication. Design decisions: text moderation = true; image video scan = true; video renditions = background; failure behavior = remain-pending.

component.highlightReason: The brief explicitly requires moderation and multiple media types.

steps.title: Request a moderation decision
steps.content: The social write service creates a moderation task for pending posts; publication waits for the task's approved outcome.

connection.label: Pending content review
connection.description: Asynchronously evaluate post policy and required media processing.

steps.title: Inspect uploaded media
steps.content: Workers read the original object, scan it, and write approved variants back to storage. They reference only the verified output keys in the post record.

connection.label: Scan and transcode
connection.description: Read pending media, produce safe thumbnails/video renditions, and report object keys.

steps.title: Approve or reject canonically
steps.content: A moderation decision updates the canonical post state. The same durable transition emits an approved-post outbox event; a failed worker can retry idempotently.

connection.label: Moderation state commit
connection.description: Mark a post approved/removed and make its publication event durable.

steps.title: Gate public visibility on approval
steps.content: Apply the publish gate: only approved content and verified media variants enter feeds. Removal or privacy changes produce invalidation events, and read-time checks protect against stale cached IDs.

decision.question: Should a pending post enter followers' feeds before moderation completes?
decision.chosenReason: It prevents a large fanout of content that policy later rejects or media that is not ready.

alternatives.tradeoff: A celebrity post can reach millions before the retraction propagates.

properties.purpose: Durable post metadata/text and interaction records with moderation and visibility state. Design decisions: partitioning = post_id-and-author-time-index; transactional outbox = true; state = pending,approved,removed. Design decisions: publish gate = moderation-approved; removal propagation = tombstone-and-cache-invalidation; visibility check on read = true.

steps.title: Add the media CDN
steps.content: Serve approved image/video variants from a CDN with access and cache policies matching post visibility. Browsers do not stream video from the post service.

component.label: Media CDN
component.description: Cache approved images and adaptive video segments

properties.purpose: Deliver approved images/video variants close to readers without loading application servers. Design decisions: adaptive video = true; visibility aware urls = true.

component.highlightReason: Large media must scale separately from feed metadata and ranking.

steps.title: Serve only approved variants
steps.content: The CDN fetches processed variants from storage; an invalidated or private post loses usable delivery authorization.

connection.label: Approved media variants
connection.description: Cache authorized image/video objects for reader playback.

steps.phase: 2. Fan out without a celebrity storm
steps.title: Choose where fanout work belongs
steps.content: An ordinary author can push a new approved post ID to followers' candidate lists. A celebrity with millions of followers must not trigger millions of synchronous writes before publication completes. Classify authors by follower count and pull celebrity posts during feed reads. Both paths keep the canonical post store as the source of truth and validate visibility at read time.

steps.phase: 2. Fan out without a celebrity storm
steps.title: Add the committed event bus
steps.content: Publish approved-post, removal, follow, and engagement events through a durable outbox. Give each consumer group its own committed offset and replay window; preserve order within an entity partition. Retry transient failures with bounded exponential backoff, then park poison events in a durable dead-letter queue for inspected redrive. Stable event IDs and entity versions make replay safe.

component.label: Social Event Bus
component.description: Committed posts, engagement, retries, and replay

properties.purpose: Buffer durable publication/engagement events for independent consumer groups. Design decisions: delivery = at-least-once; event version = true; source = transactional-outbox; ordering = per-entity-partition; consumer checkpoint = committed-offset; retry = bounded-exponential-backoff; poison events = durable-dead-letter-queue; replay = per-consumer-window; redrive = inspected-and-idempotent.

component.highlightReason: Feed materialization and trends must not hold the user write open.

steps.phase: 2. Fan out without a celebrity storm
steps.title: Publish the approved post event
steps.content: Only an approved canonical post emits the fanout event. Outbox replay prevents a crash after database commit from losing a feed update.

connection.label: Approved post / tombstone
connection.description: Publish committed post state transitions to downstream consumers.

steps.phase: 2. Fan out without a celebrity storm
steps.title: Add fanout workers
steps.content: Workers consume approved events. For ordinary authors, push post IDs into follower candidate lists in bounded batches. For celebrity authors, update only a compact author timeline and let reads merge it on demand. Commit a partition checkpoint only after the batch is durably materialized; on retry, deduplicate each event/recipient and reject stale entity versions. Bound retries, send repeatedly failing events to the durable dead-letter queue, and expose a controlled redrive path.

component.label: Hybrid Fanout Workers
component.description: Idempotent batch fanout, ordered replay, bounded recovery

properties.purpose: Materialize follower feed candidates without write-amplifying celebrity posts. Design decisions: dedupe key = event_id,recipient_id; scales on = fanout-lag; retry = bounded-exponential-backoff; poison event = durable-dead-letter-queue; checkpoint = only-after-durable-batch; replay = last-committed-partition-offset; ordering = per-entity-partition; stale updates = reject-by-entity-version; redrive = inspected-and-idempotent.

component.highlightReason: Celebrity fanout is the defining scaling trap in this problem.

steps.phase: 2. Fan out without a celebrity storm
steps.title: Consume committed social events
steps.content: The event bus feeds idempotent workers; backpressure delays freshness without blocking post creation.

connection.label: Fanout and invalidation
connection.description: Process approved posts, removals, and follow changes with bounded retries.

steps.phase: 2. Fan out without a celebrity storm
steps.title: Read follower batches
steps.content: Fanout pages through the graph for ordinary accounts instead of loading all followers into memory. Celebrity accounts are classified before expansion.

connection.label: Follower batches
connection.description: Enumerate followers for bounded ordinary-author fanout.

steps.phase: 2. Fan out without a celebrity storm
steps.title: Add per-user feed candidates
steps.content: The feed cache stores recent post IDs by reader, not the only copy of posts. Entries have bounded age and can be rebuilt. Keep candidate lists separate from final ranking, privacy checks, and post hydration.

component.label: Feed Candidate Cache
component.description: Recent per-reader post IDs and freshness watermark

properties.purpose: Serve recent ordinary-author candidates with a freshness watermark; rebuild from canonical timelines. Design decisions: key = reader_id; bounded length = true; rebuildable = true.

component.highlightReason: Cached candidates make the <200ms read plausible without making cache authoritative.

steps.phase: 2. Fan out without a celebrity storm
steps.title: Materialize ordinary-user candidates
steps.content: Workers insert post IDs into follower lists with idempotent event IDs. Visibility removals invalidate or hide cached candidates.

connection.label: Push candidate IDs
connection.description: Update bounded per-reader feed candidates for non-celebrity authors.

steps.phase: 2. Fan out without a celebrity storm
steps.title: Choose hybrid fanout
steps.content: Use a measurable starting threshold of 100,000 followers for pull-based celebrity timelines, then tune it from fanout write amplification, queue lag, and read-merge p95. Add hysteresis: switch to pull above the threshold, but switch back only below 80,000 followers for at least one hour; record the policy version so a transition cannot duplicate or omit posts. These values are initial operating assumptions, not universal constants.

decision.question: How does a celebrity post reach millions of followers?
decision.chosen: Push ordinary posts and pull celebrity posts during feed reads
decision.chosenReason: Start at 100,000 followers; tune against fanout lag and read-merge p95, with an 80,000-follower/one-hour hysteresis to avoid flapping while preserving low-latency typical reads.

alternatives.option: Push every post to every follower
alternatives.tradeoff: A celebrity creates millions of writes and a hot queue partition.

alternatives.option: Pull every followed author's posts on each read
alternatives.tradeoff: High-follow-count users incur large, variable read latency.

properties.purpose: Materialize follower feed candidates without write-amplifying celebrity posts. Design decisions: strategy = push-ordinary-pull-celebrity; initial pull threshold = 100000 followers; return-to-push threshold = 80000 followers sustained 1 hour; threshold tuning signals = fanout-write-amplification, queue-lag, read-merge-p95; threshold policy version = recorded; dedupe key = reader_id,event_id; materialized entry = conditional unique upsert; scales on = fanout-lag; celebrity timeline = compact-pull-path.

steps.phase: 2. Fan out without a celebrity storm
steps.title: Track cache freshness and removals
steps.content: Candidates are IDs only. A removal or privacy change writes a versioned tombstone and invalidation event; an urgent invalidation lane updates candidate indexes, but every read still checks canonical moderation, post visibility, and the reader’s current follow/audience version. If that authoritative check times out, fail closed and omit the candidate. A stale cache is never permission to serve old content.

properties.purpose: Serve bounded recent ordinary-author candidate IDs; never store authoritative post bodies or permissions. Design decisions: key = reader_id; rebuildable = true; candidate uniqueness = conditional(reader_id,event_id) upsert; freshness watermark = true; visibility invalidation = versioned tombstone with urgent consumer lane; follow/audience version = checked on read; stale entity versions = rejected; canonical authorization timeout = fail-closed omit; removal cache TTL = bounded; rebuild = canonical timeline.

steps.phase: 2. Fan out without a celebrity storm
steps.title: Trace the approved publish path
steps.content: The author commits a pending post and optional media; moderation approves it; the post store emits a durable event; fanout pushes ordinary candidate IDs or retains a celebrity timeline. None of those background copies is the permission authority. Follow/unfollow and removals change what a read may return even if an older candidate list remains cached.

steps.title: Add the feed read service
steps.content: Budget the <200ms p95 request end to end: gateway/auth 15ms, candidate-cache read 20ms, bounded hydration plus canonical visibility checks 40ms, parallel celebrity-timeline merge 40ms for at most 20 authors, ranking 40ms, and response reserve 40ms (195ms total). These allocations, deadlines, and author/candidate caps are provisional load-test assumptions, not values specified by the brief or validated capacity. Enforce each as a deadline, not a wish. On cache miss, query at most 500 recent canonical candidates with a 40ms deadline; if the overall budget is nearly spent, skip ranking and return a verified chronological page. Omit any item whose current permissions cannot be confirmed.

component.label: Feed Read Service
component.description: Budgeted candidate merge, visibility filtering, ranking, and safe fallback

properties.purpose: Assemble personalized feed pages from cached candidates and pulled celebrity timelines. Provisional sizing hypothesis to validate under representative peak load: pagination = cursor; latency target = 200ms p95 end-to-end; budget = gateway-auth 15ms, cache 20ms, hydration-visibility 40ms, parallel-celebrity-merge 40ms max-20-authors, ranker 40ms, response-reserve 40ms; cache-miss fallback = at-most-500-canonical-candidates with 40ms deadline; ranker over-budget = skip and return verified chronological page; permission check timeout = omit item and fail closed.

component.highlightReason: This is the <200ms path users actually experience.

steps.title: Route a feed request
steps.content: The gateway routes `/feed` to the read service independently of post creation.

connection.label: GET /feed cursor page
connection.description: Request an authenticated, paginated feed under a bounded latency budget.

steps.title: Read cached candidate IDs
steps.content: Cache hits provide recent ordinary-author IDs and freshness; a cache outage falls back to bounded canonical timelines rather than showing an empty feed.

connection.label: Recent candidate IDs
connection.description: Fetch bounded per-reader candidates and freshness watermark.

steps.title: Hydrate posts and pull celebrities
steps.content: Hydrate no more than 500 bounded candidates and fetch up to 20 celebrity timelines in parallel under a shared 40ms merge deadline. A removal tombstone or newer visibility version invalidates an older candidate; do not wait on an unbounded celebrity fanout. Re-check moderation, deletion, follow and audience permissions against canonical state before ranking. If the authoritative permission lookup times out, omit the item rather than risk a privacy leak.

connection.label: Hydrate / pull author timeline
connection.description: Fetch bounded approved posts and parallel celebrity timelines; enforce current moderation, tombstone, and visibility versions.

steps.title: Check follows and audience policy
steps.content: The graph identifies followed celebrity authors and verifies that a candidate is still visible to this reader after follow/privacy changes.

connection.label: Follow and visibility check
connection.description: Resolve followed authors and current audience permissions before ranking.

steps.title: Add a ranking service
steps.content: Rank a bounded, authorized candidate set using freshness, follow affinity, and engagement signals. Keep model/feature retrieval within a timeout and never let a ranking failure bypass visibility checks.

component.label: Feed Ranker

properties.purpose: Score visible candidates using freshness and user-interest features within a strict timeout. Design decisions: feature signals = follows,engagement,freshness; fallback = chronological; candidate limit = 500.

component.highlightReason: Personalization is required, but ranker failure must not take down the feed.

steps.title: Rank only visible candidates
steps.content: The read service supplies authorized candidates to the ranker; ranking outputs IDs and scores, not a permission decision.

connection.label: Rank bounded candidates
connection.description: Personalize a prefiltered set under an explicit timeout.

steps.title: Choose a safe read fallback
steps.content: Treat the 195ms stage split, author/candidate caps, and sub-deadlines as provisional hypotheses to validate under representative peak load: gateway/auth 15ms, cache 20ms, hydration plus permission checks 40ms, up to 20 parallel celebrity timelines within 40ms, ranking 40ms, and response reserve 40ms. Bound cache-miss fallback to 500 canonical candidates and 40ms. If the ranker misses its 40ms deadline or earlier stages consume the remaining budget, cancel optional work and return the current verified chronological page. If current moderation or audience permissions cannot be confirmed, omit the candidate; never fall back to raw IDs.

decision.question: What should happen when a read dependency or personalized ranking exceeds its deadline?
decision.chosen: Return a bounded, visibility-verified chronological page within the remaining request budget
decision.chosenReason: It protects the <200ms p95 target without turning a cache, graph, or ranker outage into a privacy leak.

alternatives.option: Wait indefinitely for the model or celebrity timelines
alternatives.tradeoff: Violates the latency objective and makes hot-author load unbounded.
Can leak removed or newly private posts.

properties.purpose: Assemble personalized cursor pages from bounded cached candidates and pulled celebrity timelines. Design decisions: visibility = canonical moderation/post/follow-audience check on every read; latency target = 200ms p95; stage budgets = gateway-auth 15ms, candidate-cache 20ms, hydration-visibility 40ms, parallel celebrity merge 40ms max-20-authors, ranker 40ms, response reserve 40ms (195ms total); these values are not brief requirements or validated capacity; candidate cap = 500; cache-miss fallback = 40ms bounded canonical lookup; ranker deadline = 40ms; budget exhausted = cancel optional work and return verified chronological page; permission lookup timeout = fail-closed omit; never return raw cache IDs.

steps.title: Add reader devices
steps.content: Readers receive a cursor page of text plus media URLs. Live notifications later tell them that new content is available; they fetch a new feed page rather than trusting an unfiltered push payload.

component.label: Reader Web & Mobile
component.description: Paginated personalized feed and media playback

properties.purpose: Render authorized ranked feed pages, receive new-post hints, and fetch media from CDN. Design decisions: pagination = cursor; live refresh = true.

component.highlightReason: The visible feed response is the product outcome, not the fanout queue.

steps.title: Return the personalized page
steps.content: The read service returns a bounded cursor page with freshness information and safe media references.

connection.label: Ranked feed page
connection.description: Return visible posts and the next cursor within the feed latency budget.

steps.title: Load approved media from CDN
steps.content: Readers fetch images and video segments independently of feed metadata. Private media uses scoped authorization and invalidation on visibility changes.

connection.label: Image / video playback
connection.description: Serve approved media variants without slowing feed assembly.

steps.title: Persist likes, comments, and shares
steps.content: Apply the engagement contract to the social write service: idempotent likes, durable comments, and shares that create a reference to an approved post. Counters may lag, but the interaction record is durable and unauthorized users cannot act on private content.

properties.purpose: Validate and durably apply post, follow, like, comment, and share commands. Design decisions: idempotency key = user_id,client_operation_id; write models = post,follow,like,comment,share. Design decisions: likes = idempotent-user-post-record; comments = durable-moderated-record; shares = authorized-post-reference; engagement counters = eventual.

steps.title: Publish engagement changes
steps.content: Committed likes/comments/shares feed ranking features and trends asynchronously. The user write returns after its own durable commit, not after global recomputation.

connection.label: Engagement / follow event
connection.description: Publish committed interactions for cache invalidation, ranking features, and trend aggregation.

steps.title: Add real-time feed hints
steps.content: A notifier consumes approved-post events and sends a lightweight new-content hint to connected readers. It does not bypass moderation/privacy or push a full pre-ranked feed; clients request a fresh page.

component.label: Realtime Feed Notifier
component.description: New-post hints over WebSocket or SSE

properties.purpose: Notify online readers that an approved feed update may be available. Design decisions: transport = WebSocket-or-SSE; payload = new-content-hint; offline behavior = next-feed-read.

component.highlightReason: Real-time updates are required, but the read service remains the authorization boundary.

steps.title: Consume update events
steps.content: Notifier instances coalesce bursts so a celebrity event does not send an unbounded number of socket writes at once.

connection.label: Approved update hint
connection.description: Turn committed post changes into bounded live refresh signals.

steps.title: Notify active readers
steps.content: A connected reader sees a new-post hint and explicitly refetches a filtered feed page; offline readers see updates on their next read.

connection.label: New content available
connection.description: Send a lightweight live refresh hint, not unfiltered post content.

steps.title: Add trending aggregation
steps.content: Count hashtags and engagement in bounded time windows. Deduplicate events, filter known spam/bots, and keep trend computation off the feed read path. Location-specific trends can use privacy-safe coarse regions.

component.label: Trending Aggregator

properties.purpose: Compute time-windowed, abuse-filtered trending hashtags from committed events. Design decisions: windowing = rolling-time-buckets; dedupe key = event_id; consistency = eventual.

component.highlightReason: Trending topics are a required read feature but not a synchronous post-write obligation.

steps.title: Consume hashtags and interactions
steps.content: The same committed bus feeds trend workers; a lagging trend view does not delay feed delivery.

connection.label: Hashtag / engagement events
connection.description: Aggregate approved post tags and validated engagement events by time window.

steps.title: Add the trend view store
steps.content: Serve top topics/hashtags from rebuildable aggregates. Mark the result with an updated-at timestamp and retain enough raw event history for recovery.

component.label: Trend View Store
component.description: Rebuildable top hashtags and time-window counts

properties.purpose: Serve current trending topics and hashtags from aggregated approved events. Design decisions: consistency = eventual; updated at = true.

component.highlightReason: Trend reads need a cheap materialized view, not a full scan of all posts.

steps.title: Persist trending windows
steps.content: Workers write versioned time-window aggregates that can be rebuilt from retained events.

connection.label: Trending hashtag windows
connection.description: Write top topics and counts for a cheap trending API read.

steps.title: Add feed operating signals
steps.content: Observe feed p95/p99, cache hit ratio, consumer lag, oldest unprocessed event age, fanout catch-up rate, dead-letter depth, celebrity pull cost, moderation backlog, ranking timeout, media failures, and trend freshness. Treat 30 seconds as a provisional lag threshold to tune against the freshness objective and measured traffic; alert on sustained DLQ growth; at 1B DAU, a healthy write API can hide stale downstream projections.

component.label: Feed & Fanout Monitoring
component.description: Latency, lag, replay rate, dead letters, and freshness

properties.purpose: Alert on feed latency, fanout backlog, hot authors, privacy invalidation, moderation lag, dead-letter growth, replay/catch-up rate, and trend freshness. Design decisions: feed latency target ms = 200; daily active users target = 1000000000; feed consumer lag alert threshold is provisional and must be calibrated; monitor oldest event age = true; monitor catch-up rate = true; monitor dead-letter depth = true.

component.highlightReason: The <200ms and 1B-DAU claims need observable bottleneck and failure signals.

steps.title: Export fanout and freshness metrics
steps.content: Observe the event bus and downstream consumers separately so a healthy write API does not hide a stale feed.

connection.label: Lag and freshness SLOs
connection.description: Emit consumer lag, event age, fanout backlog, and invalidation failures.

steps.title: Recover from sustained event backlog
steps.content: When consumer lag exceeds 30 seconds or the oldest event keeps aging, alert and scale consumers up to the partition limit; throttle ordinary fanout batch size and keep celebrity posts on the pull path. Pause only nonessential trend/live-hint work if necessary, never visibility enforcement. Resume each consumer from its own last committed offset in partition order. Materialization uses a conditional unique (reader_id,event_id) upsert, so at-least-once retries become no-ops; write the durable batch before committing its offset. Reject replays older than the seven-day candidate window except versioned removal tombstones. Route poison events to the DLQ, inspect and repair them, then redrive idempotently. Read-time canonical permission checks and tombstones keep removed/private posts hidden while projections catch up.

scaleTrigger.metric: feed_consumer_lag_s >= 30 or oldest_unprocessed_event_age_s increasing or dead_letter_depth increasing
scaleTrigger.action: Alert; scale consumers within partition limits; throttle fanout batches; pause only nonessential trend/live-hint groups; replay each consumer from its committed partition offset in order; conditionally upsert unique recipient/event entries; commit offsets after durable writes; inspect and idempotently redrive DLQ events
scaleTrigger.impact: Restores freshness without lost/duplicate feed entries or user-write stalls; current authorization checks fail closed while invalidations catch up.

properties.purpose: Materialize follower feed candidates without write-amplifying celebrity posts. Design decisions: strategy = push-ordinary-pull-celebrity; initial pull threshold = 100000 followers; return-to-push threshold = 80000 followers sustained 1 hour; threshold tuning signals = fanout-write-amplification, queue-lag, read-merge-p95; threshold policy version = recorded; dedupe key = conditional-unique(reader_id,event_id); candidate TTL and replay window = 7 days; duplicate replay = no-op; scales on = fanout-lag; retry = bounded-exponential-backoff; poison event = durable-dead-letter-queue; checkpoint = only-after-durable-batch; replay = last-committed-partition-offset in per-entity-partition order; stale updates = reject-by-entity-version; removals = versioned tombstone; recovery = scale-within-partition-limit, throttle-ordinary-batch, pause-only-nonessential-consumers, inspected-idempotent-redrive; celebrity path = compact-pull-timeline.

steps.title: Read trends through the feed service
steps.content: The trend aggregator writes asynchronously; readers query a bounded time window through the feed service. Keep this read independent of regular feed assembly and apply current moderation, visibility, and locale policy before returning topics.

connection.label: GET /trending view lookup
connection.description: Read an eventual trend window through the service; never expose the store directly to clients.

steps.title: Set the trend endpoint and safety checks
steps.content: Return a bounded, eventually consistent trend list only after the current policy checks; do not assume an aggregate counter overrides a post removal or privacy change. Keep the personalized feed’s full 195ms stage budget and fail-closed fallback unchanged.

properties.purpose: Assemble personalized cursor pages from bounded cached candidates and pulled celebrity timelines. Design decisions: visibility = canonical moderation/post/follow-audience check on every read; latency target ms = 200; SLO = p95; stage budgets = gateway-auth 15ms, candidate-cache 20ms, hydration-visibility 40ms, parallel celebrity merge 40ms max-20-authors, ranker 40ms, response reserve 40ms (195ms total); candidate cap = 500; cache-miss fallback = 40ms bounded canonical lookup; ranker deadline = 40ms; budget exhausted = cancel optional work and return verified chronological page; permission lookup timeout = fail-closed omit; never return raw cache IDs; trending endpoint = GET /trending?window=...; trend consistency = eventual; trend visibility checks = current moderation-and-permissions.

steps.title: Review the five product flows
steps.content: **Post/media:** social API → pending canonical post + scoped media → processing/moderation → approved event. **Follow:** update graph and emit change. **Feed:** cached ordinary candidates + pulled celebrity timelines → current visibility/moderation check → bounded personalization → <200ms target page. **Engage:** durable likes/comments/shares produce async counters/ranking/trends events. **Realtime:** approved events yield refresh hints. **Trends:** the service reads an eventually consistent window from the trend view after current moderation and privacy checks. A deleted/private post must disappear from feeds even if a stale candidate or aggregate remains temporarily.
